List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

Total number of questions — 20
Restructuring of 20 Point
Programme
*21 SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of STATISTICS AND
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to restructure 20 Point Programme;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the objectives of the 20
Point Programme are yet to be achieved;
and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Vacant posts  in Doordarshan
*22. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that posts of
crucial decision making officers like Chief
Executive Officer, Member (Personnel),
Member (Finance) and Director-General,
Doordarshan are lying vacant for a
considerable time;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and by
when these posts are expected to be filled
up;
(c) whether it is also a fact that vacancies
on the board are reflecting on the functioning
of Prasar Bharati;
(d) if so, whether any action plan has
been envisaged to overcome the situation; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Road development proposals from
Andhra Pradesh
*23. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received

8
any proposals  from the State of Andhra
Pradesh during the current year for up-
gradation, improvement and development
of National Highways;
(b) if so, the road-wise, National
Highway-wise details thereof; and
(c) the total funds allocated and
expenditure made by Government for the
development, up-gradation, improvement
and construction of various roads and
National Highways?
Process of poverty estimation
*24. SHRIMATI MOHSINA KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the entire process of poverty estimation
by the Planning Commission is
characterized by arbitrariness and gross
under estimation;
(b) whether it is a fact that there are
different agencies for devising poverty
criteria like Ministry of Rural Development
and States determining BPL status; and
(c) whether Government would fix
uniform criteria for determination and
identification of poor people for having
estimates of BPL people in the country?
Cost overrun in pending Government
projects
*25. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME
IMPLEMENTATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a cost overrun
of more than 10 per cent in 315 pending
Government projects, costing over Rs. 100
crore each;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for not completing projects in the
estimated time, State-wise;
(c) whether his Ministry is monitoring
the projects to ensure their smooth
completion; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Indians in Pakistani jails
†* 26. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of Indians are
detained in Pakistani jails, if so, the reasons
for keeping them in prisons;
(b) the approximate number thereof and
since how many years they are imprisoned;
and
(c) whether Government have taken any
action to get these prisoners released and if
so, the results thereof and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Scheme for franchising postal outlets
*27. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Department of Posts
have issued orders for the launch of the
scheme for franchising postal outlets in
urban areas in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
number of such outlets notified State-wise;
and
(c) the reasons for the franchising of
postal jobs?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

9
 Urban infrastructure development
schemes
*28. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of various schemes
formulated and being implemented by
Government for urban infrastructure
development in the country;
(b) the details of funds allotted for the
purpose by Government during the last
three years; and
(c) the details of achievements made so
far in this regard?
Repair and maintenance of NHs in

Total number of questions — 143

Performance of the country in sports
101. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the country is losing rapidly in sports;
(b) if so, the details of the international
games, where India has been defeated during
the last one year;
(c) the persons responsible for such a
poor training and instructions to the players;
and
(d) the steps being taken to improve
the games performance in the country in
view of the international status of the
country?
Scruitiny of Indo-US Nuclear deal by
AEC
102. SMT SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Atomic
Energy Commission would scrutinize the
Indo-US Civilian Nuclear Agreement once
it is approved by the US Senate and
Congress;
(b) if so, whether this exercise would
enable concerns raised by the political
parties resolved at that point of time, when
the US Parliament had already approved
the Agreement; and
(c) how the assertion of the AEC that
"We (AEC) will not allow any one to take
India for a ride" would get actually
translated?
Setting up four new sites for nuclear
generation
103. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Nuclear Power
Corporation of India propose to set up
additional nuclear generation capacity
plants of 6,000 to 10,000 mw on the four
new sites;

25
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether such a project is also
proposed to be set up in Orissa; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Nuclear power through private sector
104. SHRI PRASANTA CHATTER-
JEE: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have sought reforms in nuclear power sector
through private sector participation; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Selling of Uranium to India
*105. SHRIMATI N. P. DURGA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Australia has
agreed in principle to sell Uranium to India;
(b) if so, the details of the move;
(c) whether any request has been made
to this extent by India to Australia;
(d) whether it is also true that Australia
putting some conditions to sell Uranium to
India;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) whether the conditions affect India's
prospects of getting Uranium?
Handling over of coal mining
106. SHRI YASHWANT SINHA:
SHRI SHATRUGHAN SINHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to handover coal mining to the private
sector; and
(b) if so, the total quantity of coal
proposed to be set up apart for this
purpose, and the number of private
players, who have so far been given or are
proposed to be given coal mines for mining
purposes?
Planning to buy coal mines abroad
107. SHRI S. M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have bought
coal mines abroad directly or through PSUs
coal companies;
(b) the details of such plans, deals and
projects;
(c) whether it is necessary to buy a coal
mine to import coal; and
(d) the reasons behind the plans to buy
coal mines abroad?
Government's plan to permit coal
mining by standalone companies
108. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's plan to
permit coal mining by standalone mining
companies that have tied up firm supply
contracts with power, steel and cement
companies to become operational;
(b) whether the Law Ministry has also
accorded its nod to the proposal and mining
companies having firm supply contracts
with approved users can undertake mining
coal blocks reserved for captive users even
without amending the Coal Mines Act,
1973;
(c) if so, whether any concrete
programme or action plan has been
prepared by the Ministry in this regard;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

26
The demand-supply gap of coal
109. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
amend the 'Coal Mines Nationalisation Act'
to open up coal mining to private players
without the restriction of captive use;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that there is a
huge gap between demand and supply of
coal in the country;
(d) if so, the present demand-supply gap;
